source.title: Understanding and Preserving Safety in Fine-Tuned LLMs
source.authors: Jiawen Zhang; Yangfan Hu; Ke-Jia Chen; Lipeng He; Jia-Chen Ma; Jian Lou; Daniel Li; Jian Liu; Xiao-Hu Yang; Ruoxi Jia

page_placements.theme: Safety sensitivity depends on update direction and geometry
Replay, data selection and constraints can preserve downstream safety

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether harmful and benign fine-tuning raises harmful-request ASR, using standard SFT and safety-preserving fine-tuning on several model families and datasets.
record.gate_note: Rows record standard SFT ASR results, SPF ASR results, and the text-described deep-fine-tuning SPF result. Gradient geometry and cosine-similarity findings are recorded as findings outside the listed claim versions. The cited findings from other studies are not rows. Other defense-method comparisons in Table 2 are left out because they are comparator methods, not the standard-SFT intervention selected for the claim; HS and utility metrics are not refusal/compliance rates.
record.test_reason: Its standard-SFT baselines measure harmful-request ASR on HEx-PHI after fine-tuning three instruct models. Two settings are used: 100 harmful examples from Qi et al. (V1) and benign GSM8K or SQL data (V2). Recipe differences from the originals: open 7-8B models, HarmBench classifier judge, and 5/10/20 epochs. The paper's main contribution, the SPF defence, does not bear on whether V1 or V2 hold.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also conclude that standard fine-tuning, including on benign data, steadily erodes safety as epochs increase. They attribute this to utility gradients conflicting with a low-rank safety-gradient subspace. SPF is claimed to recover near-initial safety without utility loss, including under deep fine-tuning and jailbreaks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful and benign SFT with ASR evaluation, but tests three named instruction models, several datasets and training depths, and adds SPF; the text does not establish an exact replication of the original recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with dataset, model, fine-tuning epoch, and whether SPF is applied.

fits_no_version.finding: Safety gradients have higher top-k cumulative explained ratio than Math/Code gradients, e.g. Llama at k=10: 0.85 vs 0.45/0.35.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety-preserving gradients are lower-rank than utility-task gradients in aligned LLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Safety and utility gradients, including benign Math/Code, are mostly negatively correlated step-wise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning gradients conflict directionally with safety gradients, offering a mechanism for benign erosion.

fits_no_version.finding: A single-sample safety-gradient subspace overlaps the full-batch subspace at phi > 0.8 in Llama.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The dominant safety-gradient subspace is estimable from one refusal example.

fits_no_version.finding: Projecting utility gradients off a top-10 safety-gradient subspace (SPF) keeps ASR near initial levels during harmful and benign fine-tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Orthogonal gradient projection against a low-rank safety subspace prevents fine-tuning-induced safety loss.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the ASR results. Several gradient-geometry results are presented in figures without tabulated numeric values. The paper reports different Qwen Code SFT ASRs for epoch 5 in Table 2 (0.270) and Table 5 (0.218).
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 results for SafeTune, Lisa, BackdoorAlign, and DeepAlign are omitted as comparator-method results rather than the standard-SFT intervention recorded here. Table 5 HS results and utility metrics are omitted because they are not harmful-compliance rates. Figure 7 numeric values are not extracted; the text-described SPF ASR trend is recorded in r37-r45.

untested.parts: Only 100 harmful examples; no sweep from a few to a few hundred examples. Only 7-8B open instruct models.
Only GSM8K and SQL Create have safety numbers for standard SFT. Summary and Detection appear only in the alpha-weighted Figure 2. No identity-shifting or selected 'carefully chosen' benign data.
No per-token KL or position-wise analysis.
No prefilling or decoding-change tests. Only GCG suffix attacks appear (Table 7), not recorded as rows.
Gradient low-rank structure is measured, not localization of safety behaviour in weights or ranks.
No test of data or objective causing token-depth shallowness.
No token-depth deepening is tested. DeepAlign (Qi et al.'s deepening method) appears only as a comparator in Table 2, not as a row.

missing.what: Init vs SFT (Code, 5 epochs) ASR under jailbreaks. Example: Llama Role-Play 0.025 to 0.370 and AutoDAN 0.020 to 0.615. Benign fine-tuning amplifies jailbreak susceptibility.
GCG suffix ASR on initial models: Llama 0.216, Mistral 0.698, Qwen 0.592, vs direct 0.015/0.236/0.121.
Standard SFT on combined Math+Harm, Llama-3.1-8B, 5 epochs: ASR 0.974, HS 4.90.
Standard-SFT Harmful Score (GPT-4 judge) rises, e.g. Llama Harm 1.06 to 4.82 and Code 1.06 to 2.14. This is a second judge for the same compliance outcome.

record.verdict_notes: Only the standard-SFT baselines bear on the claim; SPF and comparator-defence results are mitigation results. Recipe differences: HarmBench classifier rather than GPT-4 judge for ASR, open 7-8B models, and epochs up to 20. One author (Ruoxi Jia) co-authored the V1/V2 original source, though this paper is not an original. There are no error bars, and small Math increases may be within noise. Qwen Code 5-epoch SFT ASR differs between Table 2 (0.270) and Table 5 (0.218). The ablation text cites 'Table 8' for safety-sample results that actually appear in Figure 8.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests 100 harmful examples, not a sweep across a few to a few hundred harmful examples.
Benign fine-tuning is tested on Math and Code; other ordinary or carefully chosen benign datasets are not tested for this claim.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Compliant-opening prefills, decoding changes, and whether suffixes or getting past initial response tokens bypass refusal.
Whether a small set of model weights or ranks carries safety behavior; low-rank gradients are measured, not safety behavior localized to weights or ranks.
Whether the data or training objective makes safety shallow across response tokens.
Training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens and tests of whether such deepened safety holds up.
